key_limitations: No timing backend ran. There are zero cycles, bytes-on-wire or bandwidth numbers in this round's results.

ONNXim's pinned source shows cross-operator scratchpad residency and core-to-core data exchange are unsupported by design (Core.cc, Simulator.cc); the simple scheduler also imposes a whole-layer completion barrier (Scheduler.cc). This is a selection risk, not an environment issue.

Capacity and slot-reuse checking in our layer uses the plan's declared static order. It is a necessary-condition check; a real interleaving backend could still overflow. It is not a substitute for observed residency.
The CPU reference ran on numpy 2.3.5 while the R13 contract pins 2.5.3 (not installable here). Recorded as an explicit deviation in the run output.
SiLU exists in ONNXim only as 'swish' inside a fused BiasAct; there is no standalone elementwise-multiply op and Cast is a Dummy no-op, so the target module's cast would be silently free.
Only M=1 and M=32 were executed; M=128 was not run.
